beats.primary: For the weight you named — a mind that won't stop racing — there is a Name.

beats.label: from `collectible_names.json` id 6, verbatim
beats.primary: The Source of Serenity

beats.label: The Cave
beats.primary: Hunted out of Mecca, the Prophet ﷺ hid in a cave with his closest friend. The searchers came so close that Abu Bakr said: if one of them looks down, he will see us. The Prophet ﷺ was unshaken.

beats.label: The Cave
beats.primary: He answered: "What do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah? Do not worry — Allah is certainly with us."

beats.label: The Cave
beats.primary: And Allah sent down His serenity upon him. The danger was still outside — the stillness inside was real.
Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort.

beats.label: catalog id 6, verbatim in full — these are the Prophet's ﷺ own post-prayer words, Sahih Muslim 591
beats.primary: O Allah, You are Peace and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, O Owner of Majesty and Honor.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ وَمِنْكَ السَّلَامُ تَبَارَكْتَ يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minkas-salam tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram

beats.label: pair-synergy beat — Name₁ deck carries it
beats.primary: As-Salam — peace itself — is the Name for what is inside you. Al-Wakeel, the second Name of your answer, is the One you trust with what is outside your hands.

sources.claim: Cave narrative; "Do not worry; Allah is certainly with us"; "sent down His serenity"
Abu Bakr's words ("If any of them should look under his feet, he would see us") + "two, the third of whom is Allah"

beats.primary: A racing mind spends the night rehearsing tomorrow. This is the Name of the One you can hand tomorrow to.

beats.label: catalog id 35, verbatim + one authored gloss line to unify the renderings the user will meet
beats.primary:
The Trustee
the Guardian you hand your affairs to

beats.label: After Uhud
beats.primary: Wounded after Uhud, the believers were warned that their enemies had gathered against them — and were told to be afraid. They were not.

beats.label: After Uhud
beats.primary: The warning only made them grow stronger in faith. They answered with one sentence: ḥasbunallāhu wa niʿmal-wakīl — "Allah alone is sufficient for us, and He is the best Protector."

beats.label: After Uhud
beats.primary: "So they returned with Allah's favours and grace, suffering no harm." The harm they had been told to fear never came.

beats.label: excerpt, marked as such
beats.primary: …And whoever puts their trust in Allah, then He ˹alone˺ is sufficient for them.

beats.label: catalog id 35, verbatim — the same words the believers spoke at Uhud, and Ibrahim at the fire
beats.primary: Allah is enough for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.
You were never asked to hold every outcome. Handing them over is not giving up — it is trust, placed with the One who holds them.

sources.verified: ✅ verified reference (wording per Khattab 3:172 "after their injury")

sources.claim: Warning "so fear them" → grew stronger → ḥasbunallāh
Same phrase spoken by Ibrahim at the fire + the Prophet ﷺ

beats.primary: You named the distance. This Name is about what happens on the other side of it.

beats.label: catalog id 27, verbatim
beats.primary: The Most Loving

beats.label: The lost camel
beats.primary: A traveler alone in the desert loses his camel — and with it all his food and water. He lies down in the shade, all hope gone.

beats.label: The lost camel
beats.primary: Then he looks up — and it is standing before him. His joy is so wild the words come out backwards: "O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your Lord."

beats.label: The lost camel
beats.primary: The Prophet ﷺ said: Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than that man was with his camel.
So seek your Lord's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. Surely my Lord is Most Merciful, All-Loving.

beats.label: catalog 27, verbatim
beats.primary: O Allah, I ask You for Your love and the love of those who love You.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ حُبَّكَ وَحُبَّ مَنْ يُحِبُّكَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka hubbaka wa hubba man yuhibbuk

beats.label: pair synergy
beats.primary: That pleasure is what the Prophet ﷺ said repentance is met with. And the way back is not yours to invent — Al-Hadi, the second Name of your answer, is the Guide.
Feeling far is one thing. Not knowing the way back is another. This Name is the answer to the second.

beats.label: catalog id 33, verbatim
beats.primary: The Guide

beats.label: Musa on the road to Midian
beats.primary: Musa fled Egypt at his lowest — a life taken, the city behind him, nothing ahead but open road.

beats.label: Musa on the road to Midian
beats.primary: He carried no certainty. Only this: "I trust my Lord will guide me to the right way."

beats.label: Musa on the road to Midian
beats.primary: What met him was not the past. It was Midian — shelter, and a family.

beats.label: excerpt, marked — final clause of a longer verse
beats.primary: …And Allah surely guides the believers to the Straight Path.

beats.label: catalog 33, verbatim
beats.primary: O Allah, guide us and make us a means of guidance for others.
Even the strongest believers ask "guide us" in every prayer, every day. Needing guidance was never falling behind — asking for it is the prayer itself.

beats.primary: For the weight you named — the sin you keep returning from — there is a Name that keeps answering.

beats.label: catalog id 11, verbatim
beats.primary: The Ever-Forgiving

beats.label: The servant who kept returning
beats.primary: A man sinned, and said: my Lord, I have sinned — forgive me. And he was forgiven. Time passed, and he fell again.

beats.label: The servant who kept returning
beats.primary: Again he asked. Again he was forgiven. And a third time — Allah answered that His servant knew he had a Lord who forgives, and He forgave him.

beats.label: The servant who kept returning
beats.primary: In the story, the loop you are ashamed of ends the same way every time — not at the sin, but at the return.
O My servants who have exceeded the limits against their souls! Do not lose hope in Allah's mercy, for Allah certainly forgives all sins.

beats.label: catalog 11, verbatim
beats.primary: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. You are the Acceptor of Repentance, the Forgiving.
beats.arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الْغَفُورُ
beats.transliteration: Rabbighfir li wa tub 'alayya innaka Antat-Tawwabul-Ghafur

beats.label: pair synergy
beats.primary: Al-Ghaffar is the forgiving that does not run out. At-Tawwab — the second Name of your answer — is about the turning back itself.

sources.verified: sahih, verified via archive; beat 2 is marked paraphrase — the hadith's full clause is "a Lord who forgives sins and punishes for them"; scholars read the ending as "so long as he keeps repenting" — beat 3 keeps the return in view

beats.primary: You think the shameful part is having to come back again. Coming back has its own Name.

beats.label: catalog id 31, verbatim
beats.primary: The Acceptor of Repentance

beats.label: The man who took a hundred lives
beats.primary: A man of an earlier nation had taken ninety-nine lives. He asked: is repentance possible for me? He was told no — and the count became one hundred. Still, he kept asking.

beats.label: The man who took a hundred lives
beats.primary: Then he was told: go to a righteous town. He set out — and died on the road, still on his way.

beats.label: The man who took a hundred lives
beats.primary: The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. And the earth was commanded to draw the town closer — he was found a single span nearer to it, and forgiven.
Then Adam was inspired with words ˹of prayer˺ by His Lord, so He accepted his repentance. Surely He is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.

beats.label: catalog 31, verbatim
beats.primary: O Allah, forgive me and accept my repentance. Indeed You are At-Tawwab, the Most Merciful.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ighfir li wa tub alayyah innaka anta at-tawwabur-rahim

beats.primary: In every one of these stories, the acceptance met the person mid-road. The turning is enough to begin.

sources.verified: sahih, verified via archive — story copy uses ONLY Bukhari 3470 details; the "scholar not monk / leave the land" details are Muslim 2766, UNVERIFIED, excluded

beats.primary: For the weight you named — the heaviness that doesn't lift — there is a Name for what is broken being mended.

beats.label: catalog id 9, verbatim
beats.primary: The Compeller — Restorer of the Broken

beats.label: Yaqub's grief, and the mending of the house of Yusuf
beats.primary: Yaqub wept for his son Yusuf — grief so heavy it took his eyesight. He carried it to one place only: "I complain of my anguish and sorrow only to Allah."

beats.label: Yaqub's grief, and the mending of the house of Yusuf
beats.primary: Then came the day a shirt arrived — the same kind of shirt that once carried false blood — and this time it carried his son's scent. "He cast the shirt over Jacob's face, so he regained his sight."

beats.label: Yaqub's grief, and the mending of the house of Yusuf
beats.primary: Sight restored. Son restored. Whole again.

beats.label: excerpt, marked
beats.primary: …do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah…

beats.label: catalog 9, verbatim
beats.primary: O Compeller, mend my brokenness.

beats.label: pair synergy
beats.primary: Al-Jabbar is the Name for what broke. Ash-Shafi — the second Name of your answer — is the Name for what still hurts.

beats.primary: Some heaviness is a wound. This is the Name the Prophet ﷺ himself called on for healing.

beats.label: catalog id 38, verbatim
beats.primary: The Healer

beats.label: Ayyub: the quietest complaint, the doubled answer
beats.primary: Ayyub lost his health, then his family. His whole prayer was one line: "I have been touched with adversity, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."

beats.label: Ayyub: the quietest complaint, the doubled answer
beats.primary: He stated the pain and named the Mercy. He demanded nothing.

beats.label: Ayyub: the quietest complaint, the doubled answer
beats.primary: "So We answered his prayer and removed his adversity, and gave him back his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us."
And He ˹alone˺ heals me when I am sick.

beats.label: catalog 38, verbatim — the Prophet's ﷺ ruqyah as the catalog carries it; cf. Sahih al-Bukhari 5743, whose wording/clause order differs slightly
beats.primary: O Allah, Lord of people, remove the illness, heal — You are the Healer, there is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ اشْفِ أَنتَ الشَّافِي لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاؤُكَ شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
beats.transliteration: Allahumma Rabban-nasi, adhhib il-ba's, ishfi anta'sh-Shafi, la shifa'a illa shifa'uk, shifa'an la yughadiru saqama

beats.primary: The answer to Ayyub was not repair. It was more than there was before the breaking.

beats.primary: For the weight you named — the fear of not having enough, of not providing — there is a Name.

beats.label: catalog id 13, verbatim
beats.primary: The Provider

beats.label: The birds
beats.primary: The Prophet ﷺ answered the fear of tomorrow with a picture: a bird, going out in the morning with nothing in hand.

beats.label: The birds
beats.primary: He said: if you relied upon Allah as He deserves to be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds — they go out in the morning empty, and return full.

beats.label: The birds
beats.primary: And the bird still goes out — reliance was never sitting still; it is going out with the weight handed over.

beats.label: composite of 65:2-3, disclosed
beats.primary: And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for them, and provide for them from sources they could never imagine.

beats.label: catalog 13, verbatim
beats.primary: O Allah, suffice me with what is lawful against what is unlawful, and enrich me by Your favor over all others.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ikfini bi halalika 'an haramik wa aghnini bi fadlika amman siwak

beats.label: pair synergy
beats.primary: Ar-Razzaq is about what reaches you. Al-Fattah — the second Name of your answer — is about the doors it comes through.

sources.verified: grade: Hasan (Darussalam); Tirmidhi's own remark: hasan sahih (verified via archive; grade displayed honestly)

beats.primary: And for the doors that look shut — the application, the job, the way forward — this is the Name of the One who opens.

beats.label: catalog id 23, verbatim
beats.primary: The Opener

beats.label: Hudaybiyyah: the shut door that was a victory
beats.primary: At Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ turned back from the Ka'bah, short of the pilgrimage they had set out for. Every door looked shut.

beats.label: Hudaybiyyah: the shut door that was a victory
beats.primary: On the road home, revelation named that very moment: "Indeed, We have granted you a clear triumph."

beats.label: Hudaybiyyah: the shut door that was a victory
beats.primary: The shut door itself was the opening — named a triumph before anyone could yet see why.

beats.label: excerpt, marked
beats.primary: Whatever mercy Allah opens up for people, none can withhold it.

beats.label: catalog 23, verbatim
beats.primary: O Opener, open for us the best of openings.
beats.arabic: يَا فَتَّاحُ افْتَحْ لَنَا خَيْرَ الْفَتْحِ
beats.transliteration: Ya Fattahu iftah lana khayral fath

beats.primary: None of the gatekeepers you fear — the interviewer, the landlord, the market — can withhold what He opens. That is what this Name means.

sources.claim: beat-1's turned-back-short-of-the-pilgrimage framing is uncontested sirah documented in Bukhari's Hudaybiyyah chapters (e.g. 2731-2732), beyond the two cited hadiths

beats.primary: You didn't find this by accident. You don't have to name what you're carrying — it is not too heavy to be known.

beats.label: ✅ DECIDED, founder 2026-07-25: Saheeh International rendering — closest cadence to the phrase the reel audience carries. Verified verbatim via quran.com API resource 20.
beats.primary: Allāh does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.
Before any Name for what hurts, there is the Name that opens the Qur'an itself.

beats.label: catalog id 2, verbatim
beats.primary: The Most Gracious

beats.label: The mother among the captives
beats.primary: Among the captives of a battle was a woman who had lost her child — searching, frantic, nursing any infant she found.

beats.label: The mother among the captives
beats.primary: When she found her own child, she took him to her chest and nursed him. The Prophet ﷺ asked his companions: do you think this woman could throw her son into a fire? Never, they said — not if she could help it.

beats.label: The mother among the captives
beats.primary: He said: "Allah is more merciful to His slaves than this lady to her son."

beats.label: excerpt, marked
beats.primary: But My mercy encompasses everything.

beats.label: catalog 2, verbatim
beats.primary: O Most Gracious, have mercy on me with Your mercy that encompasses all things.
beats.arabic: يَا رَحْمَنُ ارْحَمْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ الَّتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ
beats.transliteration: Ya Rahman irhamni bi rahmatika allati wasi'at kulla shay

beats.label: pair synergy
beats.primary: A mercy that wide is where you begin. Al-Lateef — the next Name of your journey — is the kindness working in the details you can't see yet.

beats.primary: You couldn't put it into words. The One this Name belongs to never needed them.

beats.label: catalog id 36, verbatim
beats.primary: The Subtle

beats.label: Yusuf's answer at the end
beats.primary: Betrayed by his brothers, thrown in a well, sold, imprisoned for years on a false charge — and for most of Yusuf's story, nothing looks rescued.

beats.label: Yusuf's answer at the end
beats.primary: At the end — his family gathered, the years explained — he names what had been happening the whole time: "Indeed my Lord is subtle in fulfilling what He wills."

beats.label: Yusuf's answer at the end
beats.primary: Not power. Not vindication. Subtle kindness, threaded through every wound — visible only from the far side.
Allah is Ever Kind to His servants.

beats.label: catalog 36, verbatim
beats.primary: O Subtle One, be gentle with me in all that destiny has decreed.
beats.arabic: يَا لَطِيفُ الْطُفْ بِي فِيمَا جَرَتْ بِهِ الْمَقَادِيرُ
beats.transliteration: Ya Lateefu ultuf bi fima jarat bihi al-maqadir

beats.primary: "Whether you speak secretly or openly — He surely knows best what is hidden in the heart." (Qur'an 67:13) What you couldn't say was never unsaid to Him.

beats.primary: You said no one sees it. This Name is about the One who always has.

beats.label: catalog id 46, verbatim
beats.primary: The All-Seeing

beats.label: Hajar in the empty valley
beats.primary: Ibrahim left Hajar and her baby in a valley with no people and no water. She asked one question: has Allah ordered this? Yes. "Then He will not neglect us."

beats.label: Hajar in the empty valley
beats.primary: When the water ran out, she ran between Safa and Marwa seven times, searching for anyone — "she might see somebody, but she could not see anybody."

beats.label: Hajar in the empty valley
beats.primary: No human eye saw her. But an angel struck the ground — and water broke out: Zamzam — and her running became a rite every pilgrim repeats to this day.

beats.label: excerpt, marked
beats.primary: …Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
beats.source: Qur'an 58:1 (revealed for a woman whose complaint the person in the same room could not hear)

beats.label: catalog 46, verbatim
beats.primary: O All-Seeing, You see what no one else sees. Bear witness for me in what only You know.
beats.arabic: يَا بَصِيرُ أَنْتَ تَرَى مَا لَا يَرَى أَحَدٌ فَاشْهَدْ لِي بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُهُ سِوَاكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Basir, anta tara ma la yara ahad, fashhadli bima la ya'lamuhu siwak

beats.label: pair synergy
beats.primary: Al-Baseer sees what you carry. As-Samad — the second Name of your answer — is the One you can set it down on.

sources.verified: sahih, verified via archive — beat 1 quotes Hajar's "Then He will not neglect us"; the angel's later "Allah never neglects His people" is a distinct line in the same hadith, not rendered in the deck
✅ (Name in-text; al-Mujadilah context verified via Ibn Majah 188, sahih)

beats.primary: Carrying it alone is the heaviest version. This Name means no one has to.

beats.label: catalog id 34, verbatim
beats.primary: The Eternal Refuge

beats.label: Zakariyya's hidden call
beats.primary: An old man with no heir prayed a prayer the Qur'an calls private — a hidden call. No audience. No witnesses. Only a lifetime of asking.

beats.label: Zakariyya's hidden call
beats.primary: "My Lord! Surely my bones have become brittle, and grey hair has spread across my head, but I have never been disappointed in my prayer to You, my Lord!"

beats.label: Zakariyya's hidden call
beats.primary: The answer came with a name no human had ever carried: "We give you the good news of a son, whose name will be John — a name We have not given to anyone before."
Allah—the Sustainer ˹needed by all˺.

beats.label: catalog 34, verbatim
beats.primary: O Allah, O Eternal Refuge, make me needless of all others through You.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ يَا صَمَدُ اجْعَلْنِي غَنِيًّا بِكَ عَنْ سِوَاكَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ya Samad, ij'alni ghaniyyan bika 'an siwak

beats.primary: "Needed by all" means everyone leans here — the strongest people you know included. Leaning is not weakness; it is the meaning of the Name.
